q: Which of the following is a web browser?
x: A web browser is a program used to view web pages, and Firefox is one. Excel is a spreadsheet, Windows Explorer manages files and Notepad is a text editor.

q: A computer network that covers a single building or campus is called a:
x: A Local Area Network connects computers within a small area such as a building or campus. A WAN covers large regions and a MAN covers a city.

q: Which of the following protocols is used to transfer web pages?
x: HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) carries web pages between server and browser. SMTP and POP3 deal with email, and FTP transfers files.

q: Which device connects different networks and forwards data packets between them?
x: A router reads the destination address of each packet and sends it toward the correct network. A hub merely repeats data to all ports and a repeater only boosts a weakening signal.

q: Which of the following does the term "bandwidth" refer to?
o: The physical width of a computer monitor
The total length of a network cable
The amount of data that can be transmitted per second
The size of the keys on a keyboard
x: Bandwidth is the capacity of a connection, measured in bits per second. It is not a physical dimension.

q: What does the abbreviation "WWW" stand for?
x: WWW is the World Wide Web, the collection of linked pages that are accessed over the internet using a browser.

q: Which network topology connects every device to a single central device?
x: In a star topology each node has its own link to a central hub or switch. A bus uses one shared cable, and a ring joins devices in a closed loop.

q: What is the function of the Domain Name System (DNS)?
o: It converts domain names into IP addresses
It encrypts the data sent over web pages
It assigns hardware addresses to network cards
It blocks unwanted websites for the user
x: DNS works like a phone book that finds the IP address for a name such as example.com. It does not encrypt traffic, nor assign MAC addresses, nor act as a filter.

q: A device that converts digital signals to analogue signals for transmission over a telephone line, and back, is a:
x: A modem modulates and demodulates signals. A switch connects devices in a LAN, and a scanner and plotter are peripheral devices.

q: Which of the following describes a URL?
o: The address of a web page on the internet
A type of malicious program that spreads by email
A unit used to measure computer memory
A language used to write computer programs
x: A Uniform Resource Locator gives the location of a resource, such as https://www.example.com/page. It is not malware, a memory unit or a language.

q: In a bus topology, what happens if the main cable breaks?
o: The network is split or fails
Nothing, because data uses another route
x: All devices on a bus share one backbone cable, so a break stops communication across it. The other topologies, such as a mesh, offer alternative paths.

q: Which of the following is a valid IPv4 address?
x: An IPv4 address has four numbers separated by dots, each from 0 to 255. 256 is out of range and the other options have too few or too many parts.

q: Which of these addresses uniquely identifies the network card in a device on a local network?
x: A MAC address is assigned to the network interface hardware. An IP address may change with the network and a domain name is a text name. A port identifies a service on a device.

q: The internet is best described as:
o: A single very large computer in one country
A type of application software for offices
A program that is used only for typing
x: The internet connects millions of networks globally using common protocols. It is not one computer or one program.

q: Which type of network is the internet?
x: The internet spans the whole world, so it is a very large WAN. A LAN or PAN covers a small area, and an intranet is a private network.

q: What does the "https" at the start of a web address indicate?
o: The website contains no advertisements at all
The website is stored on the local computer
The website is run by a government office
The connection between the browser and website is encrypted
x: HTTPS adds encryption (TLS) to HTTP so data cannot be easily read by others. It says nothing about adverts or who owns the site.

q: Which of the following is true about a switch in a LAN?
o: It sends every packet to all connected devices
It sends data only to the intended device
It converts domain names into addresses
x: A switch learns which device is on each port and forwards frames only there. A hub is the device that sends to all ports.

q: Which protocol is mainly used to send email from a client to a mail server?
x: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) sends outgoing mail. POP3 or IMAP are used to receive it, FTP transfers files and DNS resolves names.

q: A full mesh network connects 6 computers so that every computer has its own dedicated link to every other computer. How many links are needed?
x: A full mesh of n devices needs n(n-1)/2 links: 6 x 5 / 2 = 15. The answer 30 counts every link twice, once from each end.

q: A star network has 8 computers, each joined by its own cable to one central switch. How many cables join the computers to the switch?
x: In a star, each computer has exactly one cable to the central device, so 8 computers need 8 cables. 28 is the number of links a full mesh of 8 would need.

q: In a full mesh network of 5 computers, how many network connections (ports) does each single computer need?
x: Each computer links directly to every other computer, so it needs 5 - 1 = 4 connections. 10 is the total number of links in the whole mesh (5 x 4 / 2), not the number per computer.

q: In a simple ring network, data travels in one direction and passes through each computer in turn. What is the usual effect if one computer in the ring fails?
o: The ring is broken and the whole network can stop
Only the failed computer loses its connection
Data is sent around the ring the other way
The network speed increases for the rest
x: In a simple ring every computer passes data on to the next, so one failed computer breaks the loop for all. 'Only that computer is affected' describes a star network when one of its cables fails.

q: In a star network, the cable between one computer and the central switch is cut. What is the effect?
o: All the computers lose their Internet link
Only that computer loses its connection
Every other computer slows down by half
x: Each computer in a star has its own cable to the centre, so a cut cable isolates only that computer. The whole star stops only if the central switch or hub itself fails.

q: Why is a terminator fitted at each end of the main cable in a bus network?
o: To boost the signal so it travels further
To connect the bus to the Internet
To give each computer its own address
To absorb the signal so it does not bounce back
x: A terminator absorbs the signal at the end of the backbone so it is not reflected back along the cable and does not disturb other data. Boosting a weak signal is the job of a repeater.

q: In a client-server network, which computer stores shared files and provides services to the other computers?
x: The server holds shared resources and answers requests. A client (workstation) is a computer that sends requests to the server and uses its services.

q: Five friends in a small office share files directly from each other's computers. There is no central server and each computer can both share and use resources. This is a:
x: In a peer-to-peer network every computer is equal and can act as both client and server, with no dedicated server. A client-server network has a central server providing the services.

q: Which of these is an advantage of a client-server network over a peer-to-peer network?
o: It is cheaper because no special server is needed
Every computer has equal control over all resources
Security and backups can be managed centrally on the server
It keeps working normally even if the server fails
x: With a central server, the administrator controls user access and backs up data in one place. Needing no special server and all computers being equal are features of peer-to-peer, and a client-server network depends on its server.

q: A bank connects the computers in its branches spread across one city, such as Lahore. This network is best described as a:
x: A Metropolitan Area Network covers a city. A LAN covers only a building or campus, too small for branches spread across a city.

q: A company links its offices in Karachi, Dubai and London into one network. This network is a:
x: A Wide Area Network spans countries or continents. A MAN covers one city, so it cannot join offices in three countries.

q: Which list puts the network types in order from the smallest area covered to the largest?
x: A LAN covers a building or campus, a MAN covers a city and a WAN covers countries or the world. Putting MAN before LAN swaps the two smaller types.

q: A bank wants data to keep flowing between its main servers even if any one link between them fails. Which topology best meets this need?
x: In a mesh each device has several paths to the others, so data can take another route when one link fails. A star depends on its central device, a bus on its single backbone, and a simple ring breaks when one link fails.

q: What is the main disadvantage of a full mesh topology?
o: A single cable break stops the whole network
All data must pass through one central device
It needs a large amount of cabling and is costly
Only two computers can be connected at a time
x: Every device links to every other, so the number of cables and ports grows quickly and the cost is high. A single break stopping everything is the weakness of a bus, not a mesh.

q: In which topology are all computers attached to one shared backbone cable with a terminator at each end?
x: A bus topology uses a single main cable that all devices tap into, with terminators at both ends. A star uses a central device instead of a shared cable.

q: In which topology is each device connected to exactly two neighbouring devices so that the links form a closed loop?
x: A ring joins each device to the next and the last back to the first, making a loop where every device has two neighbours. A bus is an open line with two ends, not a loop.

q: A ring network has 7 computers. How many links (cable sections) form the ring?
x: In a ring every computer links to the next and the last joins back to the first, so n computers need n links: 7. Six would leave the loop open, like a line.

q: Ten computers are to be networked. How many more links does a full mesh need than a star in which each computer has one cable to a central switch?
x: Full mesh: 10 x 9 / 2 = 45 links. Star: 10 cables. Difference: 45 - 10 = 35. The answer 45 is the mesh total, not the difference.

q: In a star network, computer P sends a file to computer Q. Through which part does the data pass?
o: A terminator at the cable end
x: In a star all traffic between computers goes through the central device. Passing through every computer in turn describes a ring, and a backbone with terminators describes a bus.

q: Ali's laptop asks the college server for his result page and the server sends it back. In this exchange, Ali's laptop is acting as the:
x: The computer that requests a service is the client, and the computer that provides it is the server. Here the college computer provides the page, so it is the server.

q: A school computer lab has 30 PCs in one room, each joined by its own cable to one switch. This is best described as a:
x: One room is a small area, so it is a LAN, and every PC having its own cable to a central switch is a star. A bus would use a single shared cable instead of separate cables.

q: How many layers does the OSI reference model have?
x: The OSI model has seven layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation and Application.

q: Which OSI layer decides the path that packets take from one network to another, using logical (IP) addresses?
x: The Network layer handles logical addressing and routing between networks. The Data Link layer moves frames within one network using MAC addresses.

q: Which OSI layer packs data into frames and uses MAC (physical) addresses to deliver them within the same local network?
x: The Data Link layer frames the data and uses MAC addresses for delivery on the local link. The Physical layer only sends raw bits and does not read addresses.

q: Which OSI layer is responsible for translating data formats, encryption and compression?
x: The Presentation layer puts data into a form both sides understand, and it encrypts and compresses data. The Application layer provides network services such as e-mail and file transfer to the user's programs.

q: Which OSI layer sets up, manages and ends the dialogue (session) between two applications?
x: The Session layer opens, controls and closes communication sessions between applications. The Transport layer handles end-to-end delivery of segments, not dialogue control.

q: Which OSI layer provides end-to-end delivery, breaks messages into segments and resends lost data, and is where TCP works?
x: The Transport layer gives reliable process-to-process delivery, segmentation and error recovery; TCP and UDP are its protocols. The Network layer routes packets but does not guarantee delivery.

q: Counting the Physical layer as layer 1, which OSI layer is layer 3?
x: From the bottom: 1 Physical, 2 Data Link, 3 Network, 4 Transport. The Transport layer is layer 4, one above.

q: At the sending computer, data moves down through the OSI layers. After it leaves the Presentation layer, which layer does it reach next?
x: Top to bottom the order is Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link, Physical, so after Presentation comes Session. Application is above Presentation, so data has already passed through it.

q: Which OSI layer deals with sending raw bits as electrical, light or radio signals through cables and connectors?
x: The Physical layer covers the medium, connectors and signals that carry individual bits. The Data Link layer works one level higher, with frames and MAC addresses.

q: A switch forwards frames by reading their destination MAC addresses. At which OSI layer does a switch mainly work?
x: MAC addresses and frames belong to the Data Link layer (layer 2), so a switch works there. A router, which reads IP addresses, works at the Network layer.

q: Which protocol is connection-oriented and makes sure that data arrives complete and in the right order?
x: TCP sets up a connection, numbers the segments, acknowledges them and resends lost ones. UDP sends data without a connection or delivery checks.

q: For a live video call, a few lost packets matter less than avoiding delay. Which transport protocol is usually preferred for such real-time traffic, and why?
o: TCP, because it resends every lost packet before going on
UDP, because it guarantees every packet arrives in order
TCP, because it needs no connection to be set up
UDP, because it sends without waiting to resend lost data
x: UDP is connectionless and does not wait for lost packets to be resent, so it adds little delay. TCP's retransmissions give reliability but cause delay, and it is TCP (not UDP) that sets up a connection and keeps order.

q: A web developer wants to upload a folder of website files from her PC to the web server. Which protocol is designed for transferring files like this?
x: FTP (File Transfer Protocol) uploads and downloads files between computers. SMTP sends e-mail, POP3 receives e-mail and DNS turns names into IP addresses.

q: How many bits are there in an IPv4 address?
x: An IPv4 address is 32 bits, written as four 8-bit numbers separated by dots. 128 bits is the length of an IPv6 address.

q: IPv6 was introduced mainly because IPv4 addresses were running out. How long is an IPv6 address?
x: An IPv6 address is 128 bits, written as eight groups of hexadecimal digits. 32 bits is IPv4, and 48 bits is the length of a MAC address.

q: To which IPv4 address class does the address 172.20.5.9 belong?
x: The class depends on the first number: Class B covers 128 to 191, and 172 lies in that range. Class C starts at 192.

q: Which of these IPv4 addresses is in a private address range (not used directly on the Internet)?
x: The private ranges are 10.x.x.x, 172.16.x.x to 172.31.x.x and 192.168.x.x, so 10.15.3.2 is private. 172.32 is just past the 172.16-172.31 range and 192.169 is not 192.168.

q: What is the default subnet mask of a Class C IPv4 network?
x: In Class C the first three octets are the network part, so the mask is 255.255.255.0. 255.255.0.0 is the default mask for Class B.

q: A Class C network uses the mask 255.255.255.0, leaving 8 bits for hosts. How many addresses can be given to hosts?
x: 8 host bits give 2^8 = 256 addresses, but the all-zeros address names the network and the all-ones address is the broadcast, leaving 256 - 2 = 254. 256 forgets those two reserved addresses.

q: The first octet of an IPv4 address is (11000000)₂. To which class does the address belong?
x: (11000000)₂ = 128 + 64 = 192, and Class C covers first octets 192 to 223. Class B ends at 191, so 192 is the first Class C value, not Class B.

q: Which hardware component must a computer have to connect to a network?
x: A NIC (network adapter, wired or wireless) connects the computer to the network medium. A graphics card drives the display and a sound card handles audio.

q: A cable run in a factory is so long that the signal becomes too weak to read at the far end. Which device regenerates the signal so the cable can be extended?
x: A repeater receives a weakened signal and regenerates it at full strength. A modem converts between digital and analogue signals and does not exist to extend a cable.

q: An office has a wired LAN. Staff want their laptops and phones to join this LAN by Wi-Fi. Which device should be connected to the LAN?
x: A wireless access point lets Wi-Fi devices join a wired network. A hub or repeater only works with the wired signals and gives no wireless link.

q: Which device joins two segments of the same LAN and passes a frame to the other segment only if its destination MAC address is there?
x: A bridge reads MAC addresses and filters traffic between two LAN segments. A repeater or hub passes every signal on without reading any address.

q: Which device works only at the Physical layer of the OSI model and passes signals out of all its ports without reading any address?
x: A hub just repeats incoming bits to every port, which is Physical layer work. A switch and a bridge read MAC addresses (Data Link layer) and a router reads IP addresses (Network layer).

q: Which of these is written in the usual form of a MAC address?
x: A MAC address is 48 bits, written as six pairs of hexadecimal digits. 192.168.10.25 is an IPv4 address, and the others are a domain name and an e-mail address.

q: Which pair correctly matches a network device with the address it reads to forward data?
x: A router forwards packets by destination IP address. A switch reads MAC addresses, while a hub and a repeater read no address at all.

q: At which OSI layer does a router mainly work?
x: A router routes packets between networks using IP addresses, which is the job of the Network layer. A switch works at the Data Link layer.

q: How does a repeater differ from a router?
o: A repeater chooses paths between networks; a router only regenerates signals
A repeater reads IP addresses; a router reads no address
A repeater joins different networks; a router extends one cable
A repeater only regenerates signals; a router chooses paths between networks
x: A repeater works at the Physical layer and simply rebuilds weak signals. A router works at the Network layer, reads IP addresses and forwards packets between different networks.

q: A desktop PC has no network port and no Wi-Fi. What must be fitted to it so that it can join the office Wi-Fi network?
x: Each computer needs its own network interface; for Wi-Fi this is a wireless NIC. A repeater or hub is a separate network device and gives the PC no network interface of its own.

q: The word 'modem' is formed from which two words?
x: Modem stands for modulator-demodulator: it modulates digital data onto an analogue signal to send and demodulates it on receiving.

q: Television broadcasting, where the station sends and viewers only receive, is an example of which transmission mode?
x: In simplex mode data flows in one direction only. Half-duplex and full-duplex both allow data to flow in both directions.

q: With a walkie-talkie, both people can talk, but only one at a time while the other listens. This is which transmission mode?
x: Half-duplex allows both directions, but only one direction at a time. Full-duplex would let both talk at the same moment.

q: In a telephone call, both people can speak and hear at the same time. This is which transmission mode?
x: Full-duplex allows data in both directions at the same time. Half-duplex allows both directions but only one at a time.

q: In which type of transmission is each character sent separately, framed by a start bit and a stop bit?
x: Asynchronous transmission marks each character with start and stop bits, so no shared clock is needed. Synchronous transmission sends blocks of data timed by a common clock.

q: In data communication, what is the set of rules that the sender and receiver agree on for exchanging data called?
x: A protocol is the agreed set of rules for communication. The medium is the path that carries the message, such as a cable or radio waves.

q: Which statement correctly describes a digital signal?
o: It has a limited number of separate values, such as 0 and 1
It changes smoothly and can take any value in a range
It can be carried only by radio waves
It always has a higher frequency than an analogue signal
x: A digital signal jumps between discrete levels that stand for bits. A signal that varies smoothly over a continuous range is analogue.

q: A signal repeats every 0.02 seconds. What is its frequency?
x: Frequency = 1 / period = 1 / 0.02 = 50 cycles per second, that is 50 Hz. 0.02 Hz wrongly takes the period itself as the frequency.

q: In which modulation is the amplitude (strength) of the carrier wave changed according to the data, while its frequency stays the same?
x: AM varies the height (amplitude) of the carrier to carry data. FM keeps the amplitude fixed and changes the frequency.

q: A carrier wave keeps the same amplitude and frequency, but its phase is shifted to carry the data. This is:
x: Changing the phase (position in the cycle) of the carrier is phase modulation. Amplitude and frequency modulation change the strength and the rate of the wave.

q: In fibre-optic cable, data is carried as:
x: Fibre-optic cable carries light pulses through thin strands of glass or plastic. Electrical current in copper is how twisted-pair and coaxial cables work.

q: A network must run beside large electric motors that cause heavy electromagnetic interference. Which cable is best?
x: Fibre carries light, so electromagnetic interference does not affect it. Twisted pair and coaxial cables carry electrical signals that interference can disturb.

q: Why are the pairs of wires in a twisted-pair cable twisted around each other?
o: To let the cable carry light
To make the cable stronger to pull
To increase the length of copper
x: Twisting makes the noise picked up by the two wires cancel out, reducing interference and crosstalk between pairs. Light is carried only by fibre-optic cable.

q: Which cable has a central copper conductor, a layer of insulation, a braided metal shield and an outer cover, and is used for cable TV?
x: This layered build with a single central conductor and metal shield is coaxial cable. Twisted pair has pairs of insulated wires twisted together and no central core.

q: Microwave transmission between two towers needs:
o: A copper cable between the towers
A satellite for every short link
The towers to be in the same building
A clear line of sight between the antennas
x: Terrestrial microwaves travel in straight lines, so the antennas must see each other, which is why the towers are tall. No cable is needed between them.

q: A TV remote control sends signals over a short distance and must point at the TV. Which wireless medium does it use?
x: Infrared works over short distances and needs line of sight, which suits remote controls. Satellite and microwave links cover long distances.

q: Which wireless medium relays signals through a device orbiting the Earth and is useful for reaching remote areas?
x: A communication satellite receives signals from one ground station and sends them back down to another, covering large and remote areas. Infrared and Bluetooth work over short distances only.

q: A file of 40 megabits is sent over a link that carries 8 megabits per second. Ignoring delays, how long does the transfer take?
x: Time = data / rate = 40 Mb / 8 Mbps = 5 s. 0.2 s comes from dividing the wrong way (8 / 40).

q: A 2 MB (megabyte) file is sent over a 4 Mbps (megabits per second) link. Taking 1 byte = 8 bits and ignoring delays, how long does it take?
x: 2 MB = 2 x 8 = 16 megabits, and 16 / 4 = 4 s. 0.5 s comes from forgetting to change bytes into bits (2 / 4).

q: In asynchronous transmission, each 8-bit character is sent with 1 start bit and 1 stop bit. How many bits in total are sent for 100 characters?
x: Each character takes 8 + 1 + 1 = 10 bits, so 100 characters take 100 x 10 = 1000 bits. 800 counts only the data bits and forgets the start and stop bits.

q: A company that sells people a connection to the Internet is called a(n):
x: An ISP provides Internet access to homes and organisations. A browser is a program for viewing web pages and a search engine finds pages.

q: In the address https://www.example.edu.pk/admissions/fees.html, which part is the domain name?
x: A URL has the protocol (https), then the domain name of the server (www.example.edu.pk), then the path to the page. /admissions/fees.html is the path and file on that server.

q: In the web address www.example.gov.pk, which part shows that the site belongs to Pakistan?
x: pk is the country-code top-level domain for Pakistan. gov shows the type of organisation (government), not the country.

q: In the e-mail address ayesha.khan@mail.example.com, which part identifies the domain of the mail server?
x: In user@domain, the part after @ is the domain where the mailbox is kept. ayesha.khan is the user name, and com is only the top-level part of the domain.

q: Which statement correctly tells a web browser and a search engine apart?
o: A browser finds pages by keywords; a search engine displays web pages
A browser displays web pages; a search engine is a website that finds pages by keywords
A browser stores websites; a search engine connects users to the Internet
A browser is a website; a search engine is installed on the computer
x: A browser is a program that opens and displays web pages, and a search engine is a website you open in a browser to search by keywords. Connecting users to the Internet is the job of an ISP.

q: Hamza wants only pages that contain the exact phrase solar water pump, with the words in that order. Most search engines expect him to type:
x: Putting words inside double quotes asks for that exact phrase. OR would accept pages with any one of the words, and -pump would exclude pages that mention pumps.

q: Using Boolean search operators, which pages match the query `Lahore AND museum NOT fort`?
o: Pages with Lahore or museum but not fort
Pages with both Lahore and museum but not fort
Pages with Lahore, museum and fort
Pages with fort but neither Lahore nor museum
x: AND requires both Lahore and museum, and NOT removes any page that mentions fort. Pages with only one of Lahore or museum would match OR, not AND.

q: On a web page, a word or image that takes you to another page when you click it is called a:
x: A hyperlink links to another page or place. A bookmark is a saved address in the browser that the user chooses, not something on the page itself.

q: Which computer stores the files of a website and sends a page to a browser when it is requested?
x: A web server holds the site's files and answers browser requests with pages. The browser is the program on the user's side that asks for and displays them.

q: Sana e-mails a notice to 40 parents and does not want any parent to see the others' e-mail addresses. In which field should she put the parents' addresses?
x: Addresses in BCC (blind carbon copy) are hidden from the other recipients. Addresses in To or CC are visible to everyone who receives the message.

q: Which statement about websites and web pages is correct?
o: A web page is a set of related websites, and its first website is the home page
A home page is the browser program used to open websites
A website is a set of related web pages, and its main starting page is the home page
A website is a single file, and a web page is a group of such files
x: A website groups related web pages under one domain, and the home page is its main entry page. The home page is a page, not the browser program.
